takeaways.label: Logistics shock absorbed by domestic pivot
takeaways.text: Export freight costs rose to 20.9% of export sales from 10.7% in Q1 , but the company shifted domestic mix to 58% of revenue (from 45% in Q1), holding EBITDA growth at +10% YoY.

takeaways.label: ₹25–30 cr per quarter in lost export volumes
takeaways.text: The freight spike made base-cargo leather chemicals uncompetitive, wiping out that volume; management expects normalization by Q4 FY27.

takeaways.label: Chrome metal JV signed, 20%+ EBITDA margin targeted
takeaways.text: A 50:50 JV with DCX Chrome, France, will build 6,000-ton capacity in Visakhapatnam for aerospace, defense, and nuclear-grade chrome metal, with first production targeted for Q4 FY28.

takeaways.label: FY28 margin ambition set at 17–20%
takeaways.text: Management sees a path from current ~15% EBITDA margins to 17–18% (base case) or close to 20% (upside) as backward integration, product mix shift, and logistics normalization converge, conditional on chrome ore output meeting 80–90% of requirement and DMSO stabilizing.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether export logistics costs actually ease as guided, the pace of South Africa chrome ore shipments to India, and any quantification of the DMSO project’s margin profile as commissioning nears.

points.label: Export freight doubled
points.text: Shipping and forwarding expense hit 20.9% of export sales in Q2 FY27, up from 10.7% in Q1, driven by geopolitical disruption in West Asia impacting Asia-bound sea freight.

points.label: Volume loss concentrated in low-value cargo
points.text: The damage was isolated to base-cargo leather chemicals where freight represents 20–25% of selling price; value-added products (Chrome Oxide, Chromic Acid, Dichromate, Barium Chemicals) were not impacted.

points.label: Quantified lost sales
points.text: Management estimates ₹25–30 cr per quarter in lost revenue from logistics-impacted leather base cargo, a hole that persists until freight normalizes.

points.label: Domestic pivot as shock absorber
points.text: The company deliberately shifted focus to the domestic market, which contributed 58% of Q2 revenue vs 45% in Q1, providing a natural hedge that kept overall operating margins resilient.

points.label: Recovery timeline
points.text: Management expects logistics improvements in Q3 FY27, with a return to normal levels by Q4 FY27; leather base-cargo customers typically look at 5–6 month contracts, making Q4 the more realistic recovery window.

points.label: Not a loss, a diversion
points.text: The export-to-domestic shift is described as a rebalancing of a deliberately mixed market portfolio, not a permanent loss of sales; in other quarters, export outperforms domestic.

quotes.text: Hanumant Bhansali: "There has been an increase, but we have balanced it out by focusing more on domestic market in Q2, and that's where you have seen that our overall contribution from domestic market is 58% in Q2 FY27 compared to 45% in Q1 FY27."

sections.title: Chrome Metal JV: A New Margin Tier

points.label: The deal
points.text: A 50:50 joint venture with DCX Chrome, France, to establish a manufacturing facility for high-purity chrome metal in Visakhapatnam with proposed annual capacity of 6,000 metric tons.

points.label: End markets
points.text: Aerospace, defense, nuclear power, and welding electrodes; currently no manufacturer for chromium metal exists in India.

points.label: Product already shipping
points.text: The company has already started shipping to DCX Chrome’s facility in France with clear purchase orders for the next few quarters; the product is already approved.

points.label: Demand split
points.text: India demand is around 2,000 tons; 60–70% of production will be exported.

points.label: Process choice
points.text: The aluminothermic process was chosen for energy efficiency over the electrolytic route; management expects to achieve electrolytic-metal quality through a vacuum furnace step within one to two years.

points.label: Timeline
points.text: First phase of production targeted for Q4 of next financial year in Andhra Pradesh.

points.label: Margin signal
points.text: Management expects upwards of 20% EBITDA margin given the high value-added nature of the product, with a small delta between gross margin and EBITDA.

points.label: JV structure
points.text: The investment is not included in the company’s standalone ₹520 cr capex plan; it sits in a separate 50:50 JV entity.

points.label: Undisclosed details
points.text: Management declined to share the investment amount, capex, asset turn, or total addressable market figures, citing part of the information is confidential.

quotes.text: Siddartha Cherukuri: "Since it's a higher value-added product, the gross margin to EBITDA, there is not a significant delta, which means that we are looking at upwards of 20% EBITDA margin in this particular business given the value of the product."

sections.title: Backward Integration: South Africa & Chrome Ore

points.label: Mining has begun
points.text: Mining operations in South Africa have already started and are seeing very good output; the beneficiation processing plant is in the final phase of commissioning.

points.label: First shipments to India
points.text: The company is targeting to ship chrome ore material to India from Q4 FY27 onwards.

points.label: FY28 contribution
points.text: Next year (FY28) will see a significant contribution from South Africa operations, reducing reliance on third-party chrome ore.

points.label: Margin bridge
points.text: Backward integration benefits are expected to start flowing through in Q4 FY27, forming one leg of the FY28 margin recovery story alongside logistics normalization and product mix improvement.

points.label: Upside condition
points.text: If chrome ore output meets 80–90% of the company’s requirement, it becomes one of the key enablers for consolidated EBITDA margins reaching close to 20% in FY28.

points.label: Sodium dichromate
points.text: Capacity expansion already completed, now at 90,000 tons.

points.label: Strontium chemicals
points.text: Capacity already set up at approximately 12,000 tons per annum; major customer approvals received in India from those previously reliant on imports; revenue similar to last quarter at ~₹25 cr.

points.label: Strontium ramp-up
points.text: Management expects capacity utilization to reach the optimum level of 70% by next year (FY28), with higher contribution to consolidated figures in coming quarters.

points.label: Chrome oxide green and chromic acid
points.text: Incremental capacity additions of approximately 20,000 tons and 5,000–6,000 tons respectively are planned.

points.label: Product mix strategy
points.text: The company is focusing more on oxide and acid business for next year, supported by a clear purchase order from its European partner for oxide business.

points.label: Europe shipments
points.text: The company will be shipping more Chrome Oxide to its partner in Europe in coming months; Europe will contribute a larger share to revenue.

points.label: Barium business
points.text: A stable contributor with solid cash flow generation; capacity utilization at approximately 70%; gross block of approximately ₹375 cr with significant payback already recovered; no new capex planned in barium currently.

points.label: Solar power
points.text: Plan to add approximately 20 MW of solar power capacity, increasing solar generation capacity to nearly 6x current levels.

points.label: What it is
points.text: The company’s first venture into organic chemistry, expanding beyond its inorganic chemicals base.

points.label: Timeline
points.text: Expected to commence operations in Q1 of FY28, with two to three months of stabilization thereafter; customer approvals will happen in parallel.

points.label: First-year utilization target
points.text: Management is targeting close to 50–60% operating level in the first year; no timeline was given for reaching 70–75%.

points.label: Margin potential
points.text: Raw material cost is only 35–40% of revenue, making gross margins look very promising; economies of scale will define the eventual EBITDA margin.

points.label: Capex
points.text: About ₹250 cr of the total ₹520 cr capex plan is allocated to DMSO.

points.label: Deferred margin guidance
points.text: Management declined to give EBITDA margin guidance, calling it “not the right time,” and deferred to next year for visibility.

quotes.text: Siddartha Cherukuri: "It is very much possible. I mean, again we'd like to be cautiously optimistic, and it could be -- I mean, our target, I think what was on the horizon is 20% on a consolidated basis. We might as well achieve that. I mean; we remain very positive and optimistic that if things fall in place... yes could be close to even 20%."

items.title: DCX Chrome JV
items.text: VCL signed a 50:50 JV with DCX Chrome SAS (Delachaux Group, €122 million turnover) on 7-8 September 2026 for a 6,000 tpa high-purity chrome metal plant at Visakhapatnam, with first production targeted Q4 FY28, product already shipping to DCX France on a clear purchase order, and 60-70% of output slated for export. India has no domestic chrome metal maker and demand is growing 12-13% a year, so this adds a new, margin-accretive stream (EBITDA margin guided above 20%) in aerospace, defence and energy import substitution.

items.title: South Africa chrome ore mine
items.text: Mining has started at the Bonmerci complex acquired in November 2025, with beneficiation plant commissioning underway and the first ore shipment to India targeted from Q4 FY27. Chrome ore priced ₹30-35 per kg becomes captive supply for a total outlay of ₹20-25 crore, and management expects the benefit to support its 20% consolidated EBITDA margin target by FY28.

items.title: DMSO plant
items.text: The 10,000 tpa Dimethyl Sulfoxide plant, VCL's first organic-chemistry product and India's only production, is on track to start operations in Q1 FY28, with ₹68 crore of the ₹205-240 crore project already spent as of June 2026. Raw material comes from the barium plant at only 35-40% of cost, and management counts DMSO among the drivers toward 20% consolidated EBITDA margins.

items.title: Chrome oxide green and chromic acid expansion
items.text: About ₹220 crore of the ₹524 crore capex program is adding ~20,000 tons of chrome oxide green and ~5,000-6,000 tons of chromic acid at Vizag, on top of the sodium dichromate expansion to 90,000 tons, which has already completed. A clear purchase order from a European partner, plus 60-70% domestic chromic acid market share, underpins the mix shift that has already lifted value-added derivatives to ~50% of standalone chromium sales and targets ~50% gross margins by end FY27.

items.title: Strontium carbonate scale-up
items.text: India's only strontium carbonate plant, commercialized in August 2025, grew to ₹25 crore of revenue in Q1 FY27 - nearly matching all of FY26 - with utilization rising from 20-25% toward an optimum 70% by next year. Management expects ₹250-300 crore of revenue from the vertical over two years at optimal utilization, helped by a Mexico plant fire that removed ~24,000 tons of competing supply.

items.title: Barium value-added products
items.text: Barium capex is complete with ~70% utilization, and a PBS capacity addition decision is pending during FY27-28 to serve a business where VCL already holds ~60% domestic market share and approvals from MNC paint makers. The 84% EU anti-dumping duty on Chinese barium carbonate has added 4-5% margin, US tariffs exempt barium chemicals, and the division is expected to grow 15-20% with ~25% EBITDA margins.

items.title: US market expansion
items.text: The Texas subsidiary VCHEM Global began operations in October 2025, and management expects North America to rise from ~9% of revenue to 14-15% over a year or two as approvals secured during the high-tariff period convert into sales. With tariffs on chrome chemicals down from ~53%, management is confident of regaining volumes with existing clients over the next few quarters in a market it says is more margin-accretive.

items.title: Solar capacity addition
items.text: VCL is adding ~20 MW of solar across Vizag and Srikalahasti, roughly 6x current capacity, with only ₹5-6 crore of direct capex and the rest under an SPV model buying power at a fixed long-term price. Expected power cost savings of 15-20% flow straight into margins at energy-intensive chromium operations.
